question: In Italy, Article 15 of Decree-Law No 34/2023, as subsequently amended, grants a temporary derogation enabling health-care professionals to practice under qualifications obtained abroad. These arrangements have been extended until 31 December 2029. The protection of public health requires that all professionals undergo appropriate checks on their qualifications, competences and fitness to practise.

This poses questions as to the ethical and disciplinary oversight of professionals authorised under the derogation, even in the absence of registration with their respective professional bodies, as well as the actual uniformity of the safeguards offered to patients.

The repeated implementation of exceptional measures also raises questions as to their necessity and proportionality, in the light of Article 168 TFEU, Article 35 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and, within their respective scopes of application, Directives 2005/36/EC and (EU) 2018/958. Can the Commission therefore say: 1.

Whether it intends, within the scope of its powers, to ascertain whether Italy's derogation arrangements enabling health-care professional to practise under foreign qualification are compliant with EU law, and whether the extension granted until 2029 is proportionate?

What initiatives it intends to take to promote adequate checks on professional competence and effective mechanisms for ethical and disciplinary oversight, even in the absence of registration with professional bodies, so as to ensure a high and uniform standard of patient safety?
